formal_statement.lean_header:
theorem p01_t3_noGuard_recursive_running_error_bound
    (fp : NoGuardAddModel) (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → ℝ) :
    |recursiveSum fp.fl_add n v - ∑ i : Fin n, v i| ≤
      fp.u * noGuardRecursiveRunningBudget fp n v
formal_statement.plain_language: The no-guard recursive-summation error is at most u times the sum of the computed-prefix and new-input sizes from steps 2 through n.

assumptions: The input is any finite list of real numbers.
The first input is kept exact by the shared recursive-summation definition.
Each later rounded addition may perturb its earlier computed sum and its new input separately, with both local errors at most u in absolute value.
Overflow, underflow, and other exceptional machine behavior are outside the mathematical model.
informal_statement: Under the no-guard rule, the recursive-summation error is bounded by u times the sum over steps k=2 through n of the size of the computed previous sum plus the size of the new input.
paper_proof_status: Equations (5.2) and (5.3) print the accumulated local-error identity and its absolute-value bound.
informal_proof: Induct over the inputs. At each later addition, equation (5.1) makes the new error equal to the old error plus S_hat*alpha and x*beta. Bound those two new terms by u*|S_hat| and u*|x| and add them to the earlier running budget.
tier_rationale: The right side uses actual computed prefix sums. NumStability has no accumulated no-guard recursive running-budget theorem. Condition L has useful pieces, including a one-step no-guard identity and a generic local-error recurrence scaffold, but a proof still needs new no-guard state, indexing, witness, and budget bridges or a fresh full induction.

The generic local-error recurrence can organize an accumulation, but the library still lacks the no-guard recursive state, witnesses, index bridge, and exact computed-prefix budget required by equation (5.3).
